entries.input: Let $k$ be a nonnegative integer. Prove that $\sum_{j=0}^{k} 2^{k-j} \binom{k+j}{j} = 4^{k}$.
entries.name: Putnam2020A2
entries.conclusion: ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), 2 ^ (k - j) * Nat.choose (k + j) j = 4 ^ k
entries.title: Putnam 2020 A2

entries.input: Let $k$ be a nonnegative integer. Prove that $\sum_{j=0}^{k-1} 2^{k-j} \binom{k+j}{j} = 4^{k}$.
entries.name: Putnam2020A2Twin
entries.conclusion: ∑ j ∈ Finset.range k, 2 ^ (k - j) * Nat.choose (k + j) j = 4 ^ k
entries.title: Putnam 2020 A2, top term dropped
entries.rationale: A soundness twin for `putnam-2020-a2`: the sum stops one term short, dropping $\binom{2k}{k}$. The identity then fails for every $k$ -- at $k = 1$ the left side is $2$ and the right is $4$ -- but an off-by-one in a summation bound is the error a model is likeliest to wave through, which is what this measures. It states nothing the paper asked, so it cites no occurrence.
